title: Constraining Properties of Dust Formed in Wolf─Rayet Binary WR 112 Using Mid-infrared and Millimeter Observations
question: What are the properties, particularly the grain size distribution and composition, of circumstellar dust formed in the carbon-rich Wolf-Rayet binary WR 112?

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA Band 6 continuum and CO spectral line data, and measure central source flux and extended dust upper limits
recipe.method: Calibrate raw data with ALMA pipeline, concatenate three nights, image continuum with uniform and natural+taper weightings, subtract continuum with uvcontsub, and image CO isotopologue cubes with natural weighting and multi-scale tclean.
key_parameters: robust = -2 (uniform) and robust = 2 with 2" uv-taper (natural) for continuum

recipe.goal: Constrain stellar spectra and properties of WR 112 and its OB companion
recipe.method: Fit sum of PoWR model spectra for WC ('MW WC') and OB ('GAL-OB-Vd3') stars to archival unresolved photometry at lambda < 0.9 um and wind momentum ratio log(eta).
key_parameters: 6 free parameters: R_V (3.1 to 4.1 in steps of 0.1), g_OB, T_OB, T_WC, R_t, and continuous L_WC (1e5 to 1e6 L_sun)
assumptions: Milky Way extinction curve G23 with A_V = 11.0 +- 0.3 mag; Galactic metallicity; WC mass loss rate > 1.0e-5 M_sun yr^-1; wind momentum ratio eta ~ 0.13 with 1 dex uncertainty; helium mass fraction 55%

recipe.goal: Extract spatially resolved dust SEDs for 23 extended dust arc apertures
recipe.method: Define 23 annulus-sector apertures in two clean azimuthal sectors (13 in Sector I, 10 in Sector II) by locating radial profile troughs (cavities) in 21 um JWST image, mask 3-sigma background sources, integrate JWST fluxes, and compute ALMA 1.3 mm 3-sigma upper limits.
key_parameters: Sector I: 216 deg <= PA <= 256 deg (13 apertures); Sector II: 94 deg <= PA <= 134 deg (10 apertures); 20% uncertainty adopted for JWST fluxes
assumptions: Deprojected distance estimated as sky-plane distance at PA = 216 deg for Sector I and PA = 134 deg for Sector II

recipe.goal: Fit spatially resolved dust SEDs with free dust temperatures and a single grain radius
recipe.method: Perform a joint MCMC fit of modified blackbody emission across all 23 apertures treating each aperture temperature as a free parameter and sharing effective solid angles and a single grain radius.
key_parameters: 26 free parameters: Omega_eff^I, Omega_eff^II, grain radius a (-9.0 <= log[a/m] <= -4.0), and 23 temperatures T_d^(1)...T_d^(23)
assumptions: Radiative equilibrium, optically thin uniformly expanding dust, ACAR-type amorphous carbon optical constants (Zubko 1996)

recipe.goal: Fit spatially resolved dust SEDs using an equilibrium temperature grid and four grain size distributions
recipe.method: Compute radiative equilibrium temperature grid T_d(a, r) by balancing stellar photon absorption and thermal emission, then run MCMC fits to the 23 aperture SEDs for four grain size distribution parameterizations.
key_parameters: Grain radius parameters sampled in log space between 1 nm and 100 um; 4 distributions (single radius a_e; log-normal a_c, sigma_log_a; two radii a_1, a_2, f_2; power law a_l, a_u, beta)
assumptions: Radiative equilibrium, no scattering, median stellar spectrum S_*(lambda), constant grain size distribution across outer apertures, ACAR optical constants

recipe.goal: Fit spatially resolved dust SEDs accounting for stochastic heating of small grains
recipe.method: Compute grain temperature probability distributions P(T) on a 200-radius grid (1 nm to 10 um) for each aperture using DustEM, interpolate P(T) via quantile function linear interpolation, and fit the 23 aperture SEDs with MCMC for the four grain size distributions.
key_parameters: Grid of 200 grain radii from 1 nm to 10 um; four grain size distributions (single radius, log-normal, two radii, power law)
assumptions: Graphite heat capacity (Draine 2001), dust bulk density rho = 1.81 g cm^-3, ACAR optical constants (also tested ACH2 and BE types)

recipe.goal: Model the spatially unresolved infrared SED to constrain inner dust properties
recipe.method: Approximate circumstellar dust as continuous concentric spherical shells from r_in to R = 90,000 au, fix outer shell (r > r_s) to the resolved bimodal distribution, and fit three inner-region models (Models A, B, C) to unresolved archival photometry using DustEM and MCMC.
key_parameters: Outer cutoff R = 90,000 au; outer bimodal parameters fixed to a_1 = 1.247 nm, a_2 = 0.134 um, f_2 = 2.85e-5; Model A (free r_in), Model B (free r_in, r_s, f_in), Model C (free r_in, r_s, a_3, n_3/n_1)
assumptions: Spherical shell number density equals 9 times the number of dust in a 40-deg aperture of the same radial width

recipe.goal: Calculate dust production rate and evaluate physical mechanisms for grain size evolution
recipe.method: Integrate grain mass over the inferred size distributions to derive dust production rate over the 20.1 yr orbital period, and analytically/numerically evaluate collisional timescales, gas drag stopping time, radiative torque disruption (RATD), and radiation-driven sublimation.
key_parameters: Dust arc radial width = 5210 au; orbital period P = 20.1 yr; sublimation temperatures tested (e.g. 1800 K) at r = 100 to 300 au
assumptions: Dust coupled to gas at v_inf = 1230 km s^-1, dust bulk density rho_d = 1.81 g cm^-3, pure helium gas at T_gas ~ 2000 K for drag and RATD estimates

score_reason: The physical equations, software tools (CASA 6.6.1, PoWR, DustEM, emcee), laboratory optical constants, and model parameterizations are documented in high detail, and all numeric fit results are tabulated. However, the intermediate photometry table for the 23 apertures, exact aperture coordinates, and custom fitting scripts are not released.
rediscovery_reason: Both the ALMA Band 6 data and JWST MIRI data are archived under stated program codes, the data reduction and SED modeling steps are clearly specified, and the paper reports concrete numeric benchmarks (8.5 mJy central flux, 1.53e6 Jy sr^-1 upper limit, grain radii of 1.247 nm and 0.134 um, and dust production rate of 1.93e-7 M_sun yr^-1).
